When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10**, WATCH vs VIX Spike tier **2/4** MEDIUM, **60%** probability, backwardation and skew active
Price is calm while options traders pay up for protection. Trust the VIX side for timing risk, because the crash score only counts damage that has already happened and the options market prices what comes next.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime state **24**, STABLE, no regime shift vs Divergence composite ELEVATED, mother jaws **100**, **53.5%** of pairs diverging
A stable regime score and a maxed divergence reading cannot both describe the same market for long. Trust the divergence reading as the early warning, since correlations break before a regime score moves, and treat the stable label as lagging.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian **57**, ACCUMULATE vs Regime bias RISK OFF with **3** risk off signals aligned
One gauge invites buying weakness while the other leans defensive. Trust the risk off bias for sizing today, because the contrarian score is only a partial signal and no confluence is active to confirm a bottom.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is calm on the surface and stressed underneath. The Crash Index sits at 1/10, the regime score is a stable 24, and the Dow gained +2.4% over five days. Yet the VIX spike tier is 2/4 with a 60% probability, and both skew and backwardation are active. You are seeing quiet prices with expensive insurance.

The cross asset picture backs the options market. The divergence composite is ELEVATED, with 19 bearish pairs against only 4 bullish ones, and the mother jaws score is 100. The regime read is TRANSITIONAL at only 25% confidence, so nobody should claim a clear trend. For positioning, that argues for holding what you own, skipping fresh leverage, and keeping hedges in place. The contrarian gauge at 57 earns a small starter position at most, since no confluence is active to confirm it.

The main risk is that backwardation deepens and the spike tier climbs from 2/4 to 3/4. That would turn a quiet tape of rotation into forced selling. The read flips toward risk on if backwardation clears and the number of bearish divergent pairs falls well below 19.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime is TRANSITIONAL with only 25% confidence. That is a low number, so the model sees no dominant regime and the mix of signals is unsettled.

The regime state score of 24 says no shift has happened yet, but 3 risk off signals are aligned, which gives the bias a defensive tilt. In practice, you want a portfolio that works in more than one outcome: moderate gross exposure, hedges kept on, and no concentrated bet on a single regime.

The contrarian score of 57 says to buy weakness in small pieces rather than all at once. A jump in regime confidence well above 25% is the cue to commit more size in one direction.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together have started moving apart. Correlation drift is the measure of that break: how much the relationship between the two has changed from its recent norm.

Today 53.5% of the 43 tracked pairs are diverging, which puts the composite in the ELEVATED zone. The lean is bearish, with 19 bearish pairs against 4 bullish and a net bias of 15.

The biggest breaks all score 80. The MOVE bond volatility pair drifted from +0.25 to -0.50.

Stocks and long bonds went from +0.70 to -0.33, so bonds no longer cushion equity losses the way they did. Regional banks against the broad financial sector slid from +0.30 to -0.71, a sign of stress inside credit.

High beta against low volatility stocks cooled from +0.94 to +0.40. Gold miners against gold flipped from -0.16 to +0.72.

Taken together, the old relationships between assets are failing, and diversification built on them is weaker than it looks.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

No confluence is active today. VIX backwardation has not paired with credit stress, small cap drawdown, or yen safe haven flow, so all 3 combinations stay off.

That matters for how you lean. Backwardation alone is a warning about the VIX curve, and the cross asset evidence has not yet agreed on a single stress story.

You should not press a defensive bet as if the damage were confirmed. Keep hedges modest and watch for the first of the three partners to switch on.

A small cap drawdown or a spread blowout in credit alongside backwardation would turn this from a warning into a signal.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Regions are telling different stories, and the spread inside each region is wide. Asia has Australia at +0.6% over five days against Korea at -8.0%, a sharp break that points to stress concentrated in one market.

Europe has Switzerland at +4.0% against the Euro Stoxx 50 at -0.7%, which fits a rotation into defensive, high quality stocks. The US has the Dow at +2.4% against the Nasdaq 100 at -0.4%, so money is leaving growth and moving into value.

Crypto is steady, with Bitcoin at +3.2% and Ether at +2.3%, which says liquidity is not draining. For the US session, expect the Dow and defensives to hold up better than the Nasdaq.

A further drop in Korea would be the first sign that Asian stress is reaching US technology.

Forward-looking indicators · Bonferroni-validated
Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

These two gauges disagree, and the disagreement is coherent. The Crash Index at 1/10 (WATCH) measures damage already visible in prices, and there is almost none.

The VIX Spike Detector at tier 2/4 with a 60% probability measures what options traders expect next, and they expect more movement. Backwardation means near term volatility costs more than later volatility, which is what happens when traders want protection now.

Active skew means downside puts cost more than upside calls. Calm price action with that pricing is a market that sees a risk it cannot name yet.

Trust the VIX side for timing, and use the crash score as confirmation only if it climbs above 1 while the tier rises.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
